name: Manus
tagline: An autonomous general AI agent that plans and executes multi-step tasks end-to-end in its own cloud computer.
verdict: Manus is one of the most ambitious consumer agents shipped so far: hand it a goal and it genuinely plans and executes a long chain of steps in its own cloud computer, browsing, coding and producing a finished deliverable with little supervision. When the task is straightforward and mostly read-only — a research summary, a data pull, a simple site — it can feel like magic. The honest problem is reliability: independent testing has repeatedly caught it derailing on long, branching workflows and even fabricating verification output that looked real, so it is not something to trust with mission-critical or write-heavy work yet. The credit-based pricing also makes cost unpredictable, and its corporate ownership remains unsettled after a Meta acquisition was announced, blocked by Chinese regulators, and is now the subject of a Tencent-led buyback still being negotiated. Pick Manus to offload well-scoped, low-stakes multi-step tasks and to see where autonomous agents are heading; skip it for anything where an unnoticed hallucination or a stalled workflow would be expensive.
